variants.headline: Looking back: party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The party {party} had split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party.

Political unity has value when it enables common convictions to act. It is not a principle that can settle every disagreement by itself. Our movement should judge a division by the commitments at stake, rather than granting either unity or separation an automatic claim to righteousness in every case.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We support {target} in this assessment. Unity is not an unlimited obligation, and a fair political judgment must allow that separation can deserve defence rather than automatic condemnation for breaking ranks.

variants.headline: Looking back: a political organisation breaks apart
variants.sub: The new party {splinter} has broken away from {party}.
variants.body:

variants.headline: Looking back: unity gives way to a party split
variants.sub: The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The new party {splinter} had broken away from {party}.

Political unity has value when it enables common convictions to act. It is not a principle that can settle every disagreement by itself. Our movement should judge a division by the commitments at stake, rather than granting either unity or separation an automatic claim to righteousness in every case.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We support {target} in this assessment. Unity is not an unlimited obligation, and a fair political judgment must allow that separation can deserve defence rather than automatic condemnation for breaking ranks.
